articles.title: Iran and the US Agreed to Stand Down. India's 9 Million Gulf Workers — and Its Oil Lifeline — Are Watching.
articles.excerpt: A weekend of missiles and air-raid sirens in Kuwait and Bahrain gives way to a fragile promise to resume talks in Qatar on Tuesday
articles.image_caption: Satellite view of the Strait of Hormuz, the narrow waterway between Iran and Oman through which a fifth of the world's oil once passed daily
articles.nri_angle: Nine million Indians across the Gulf woke to air-raid sirens again this weekend — the ceasefire's fate directly determines their safety, their remittances, and India's economic stability.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Canada's $500 Billion Defence Spending Surge Just Opened the Door to India. Here's What's Actually on the Table.
articles.excerpt: High Commissioner Christopher Cooter describes a 'hockey stick' trajectory in military spending and a 'transformative' partnership after years of diplomatic freeze
articles.image_caption: Prime Minister Narendra Modi meets Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney, whose election reset a relationship frozen by the Khalistan dispute
articles.nri_angle: For 1.8 million Indian-Canadians, the defence rapprochement signals a stabilisation of bilateral ties that had chilled visa processing and people-to-people exchanges.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Just Flew a Field Hospital Halfway Around the World to Help Venezuela Dig Out
articles.excerpt: Operation Amistad sent two C-17s loaded with surgeons, portable ICUs and India's indigenous BHISHM cubes on a 14,300-km airlift — one of New Delhi's longest humanitarian missions ever.
articles.image_caption: Indian Air Force C-17 Globemaster III transport aircraft
articles.nri_angle: India's growing global humanitarian reach — from disaster relief in Türkiye to Venezuela — signals a foreign-policy posture the diaspora can point to as evidence of a country punching above its weight.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Just Built Its First Military Aircraft. A Private Company Did It Months Ahead of Schedule.
articles.excerpt: The Tata-Airbus C-295 completed its maiden flight from Vadodara on June 10, making it the first military aircraft ever manufactured in India by a private-sector company — with 85% of the structure built by Indian MSMEs.
articles.image_caption: First India-built C-295 transport aircraft during its maiden flight from Vadodara, Gujarat, on June 10, 2026
articles.nri_angle: For decades, India's tag as the world's largest arms importer embarrassed the diaspora. The C-295 assembly line signals a real shift — a private Indian company building military aircraft to global standards, with an ecosystem of MSMEs riding along.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Modi Signed 19 Agreements in Seychelles Today. Here's What India Got — and What It Gave.
articles.excerpt: A warship, UPI for the island nation, an extradition treaty, a space cooperation pact, 500 tonnes of rice, and a plan to build a national hospital — all in one afternoon on a 115-island archipelago.
articles.image_caption: Prime Minister Narendra Modi during bilateral talks with Seychelles President Patrick Herminie in Victoria, June 2026
articles.nri_angle: India exporting UPI to Seychelles means the diaspora's digital payment stack is becoming the Indian Ocean's default — and the strategic footprint in a region where China is spending aggressively sends a message NRIs in the Gulf and East Africa understand.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: OpenAI Just Hired the Man Who Ran Uber India to Lead Its Biggest Bet Outside America
articles.excerpt: Prabhjeet Singh will become OpenAI's most senior leader in India, a market with 100 million weekly ChatGPT users and growing faster than any other outside the US.
articles.image_caption: Wikimedia Commons image: File:OpenAI brain network visualization.png
articles.nri_angle: IIT Kharagpur and IIM Ahmedabad alumnus leads OpenAI in India, joining a lineage of Indian-origin leaders at global tech giants — and India is now OpenAI's second-largest market after the US.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The US Banned Its Most Powerful AI From Leaving the Country. India Decided It Was Time to Build Its Own.
articles.excerpt: After the Anthropic export ban exposed India's dependency on American AI, Delhi sent its IT secretary to Washington, partially won back access — and quietly accelerated a sovereign model that already speaks 22 languages.
articles.image_caption: Server racks at a high-performance computing data center
articles.nri_angle: Indian-origin tech workers who build frontier AI models at US companies now face the question of whether those tools will stay accessible to India — the Anthropic ban made that risk real.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Is Negotiating to Sell Its Fastest Missile to the UAE. The Iran War Made It Possible.
articles.excerpt: Talks to export BrahMos and the Akashteer air-defence system mark India's biggest defence pitch to the Gulf — and a direct counter to Pakistan's deepening ties with Saudi Arabia.
articles.image_caption: A BrahMos supersonic cruise missile launcher on display during India's Republic Day parade in New Delhi
articles.nri_angle: 3.4 million Indians in the UAE stand to benefit from a deeper defence relationship that strengthens bilateral ties and India's strategic standing in the Gulf.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India and the US Say a Trade Deal Is Days Away. Here's What's Actually Holding It Up.
articles.excerpt: Greer flew to Delhi, Goyal flew to London, and both sides called it 'very, very close.' But the Supreme Court ruling, Section 301, and a July 24 deadline are making the final stretch harder than the first mile.
articles.image_caption: India's Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal, who has led trade negotiations with the United States
articles.nri_angle: A trade deal would lower tariffs on Indian goods in the U.S. and ease diplomatic tensions affecting visa policy and the business environment for Indian-American entrepreneurs.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: NASA's Chief Just Offered to Help India Build Its Own Space Station. India Hasn't Said Yes.
articles.excerpt: Bill Nelson's India visit confirms an ISRO astronaut will fly to the ISS by 2027. The bigger question is whether New Delhi wants American help on the station it plans to build by 2035.
articles.image_caption: NASA astronaut Raja Chari with ISRO officials at Johnson Space Center, reflecting deepening US-India space ties
articles.nri_angle: Indian-American scientists and engineers at NASA have shaped US space exploration for decades; a deeper ISRO-NASA partnership creates new opportunities for Indian space startups and strengthens the technology bridge between both countries.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Europe's Worst Heatwave on Record Has Killed Over 1,000 in France. Two Million Indians Live in Its Path.
articles.excerpt: Scientists say the 40°C-plus temperatures shattering records from Germany to Britain would have been 'virtually impossible' without climate change. The same forces are weakening India's monsoon.
articles.image_caption: Satellite thermal image showing hot surface temperatures across Europe during the record-breaking June 2026 heatwave
articles.nri_angle: Over two million people of Indian origin live across Europe, concentrated in the UK, Germany, and France — the countries hardest hit by the heatwave. The same climate forces weakening India's monsoon are driving Europe's deadly heat.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Meta Just Paid $900 Million for an Indian Fintech. Its Founder Will Now Run WhatsApp.
articles.excerpt: Kunal Shah built CRED from $1 million of his own money into a $4.5 billion company. Now he's taking over the world's biggest messaging platform — and Meta's biggest bet on payments.
articles.image_caption: Kunal Shah, founder of CRED, who will lead WhatsApp globally
articles.nri_angle: An Indian founder with no Silicon Valley pedigree now leads one of the world's most important platforms, while the deal reshapes WhatsApp payments for 500 million Indian users.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Biggest Trade Deal Goes Live in 17 Days. It Has Deployed 1,000 People to Make Sure Nobody Misses It.
articles.excerpt: The India-UK CETA takes effect on July 15, cutting tariffs on everything from whisky to automobiles. For Indian professionals in Britain, it also means five years of not paying into a pension system they may never use.
articles.image_caption: India's Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal, who called the UK trade deal India's most comprehensive ever
articles.nri_angle: Indian professionals in the UK get a five-year exemption from British social security payments, saving thousands of pounds that can go into tax-free Indian provident funds instead.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Brooklyn Judge Just Told the Trump DOJ It Can't Walk Away From the Adani Case Without Explaining Itself
articles.excerpt: Judge Garaufis called the government's motion to dismiss the $250 million bribery indictment 'terse, bland, and conclusory' and ordered prosecutors to justify the decision by July 13
articles.image_caption: Gautam Adani, chairman of the Adani Group, faces unresolved criminal charges in a Brooklyn federal court
articles.nri_angle: Millions of NRI investors hold Adani Group shares through Indian mutual funds and direct equity; the unresolved US criminal case adds regulatory uncertainty to their portfolios at a time when India-US trade talks are nearing a landmark agreement.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Ireland Beat India for the First Time in Thirty Years of Trying. The World Champions Lost by 34 Runs.
articles.excerpt: Belfast's Civil Service Cricket Club hosted one of the biggest upsets in T20I history as Ireland dismantled India's post-World Cup line-up. The second T20I is today.
articles.image_caption: India captain Shreyas Iyer, who took over the T20I leadership after Suryakumar Yadav was dropped, faces early scrutiny after the historic defeat in Belfast
articles.nri_angle: Tens of thousands of Indian-origin cricket fans in the UK and Ireland follow India's away tours passionately; the historic defeat at a tiny Belfast ground — and the ongoing second T20I today — is a major talking point across diaspora WhatsApp groups and community cricket clubs.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Amazon Just Committed $48 Billion to India. Most of It Will Be Spent Building the AI Infrastructure Indians Haven't Seen Yet.
articles.excerpt: CEO Andy Jassy met Modi in New Delhi and announced $13 billion in fresh AI and cloud spending — the largest single technology commitment India has ever received.
articles.image_caption: Amazon CEO Andy Jassy, who announced a $48 billion investment commitment to India
articles.nri_angle: Indian tech professionals in the US who work at Amazon and AWS now have a concrete reason to consider reverse migration — or at least to watch India's cloud market explode from $48 billion in fresh capital.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Hyderabad Named a Road After Trump. His Own Allies in India Called It Hypocrisy.
articles.excerpt: A Congress-ruled state honours the US president with 'Donald Trump Avenue' near the US Consulate — while accusing Modi of being too soft on him.
articles.image_caption: US President Donald Trump, who thanked India for naming a Hyderabad road after him
articles.nri_angle: For NRIs from Hyderabad — and there are hundreds of thousands of them, particularly in the US tech industry — the irony of their city naming a road after a president who has raised tariffs on Indian goods, whose navy killed Indian sailors, and whose immigration policies threaten H-1B holders is impossible to miss.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Directs ONGC to Build $1.6 Billion Strategic Oil Reserve as Iran War Exposes Eight-Day Vulnerability
articles.excerpt: The new underground cavern at Mangaluru would raise India's emergency crude storage by a third, but still leaves the country far short of the IEA's 90-day standard
articles.image_caption: An underground strategic petroleum reserve storage facility. India is racing to expand its own crude oil reserves at Mangaluru, Karnataka, after the Iran war exposed its energy vulnerability.
articles.image_credit: Wikimedia Commons / US Department of Energy / Public Domain
articles.nri_angle: India's energy vulnerability directly affects NRI families through rising fuel and food prices during supply shocks, while the country's $1.6 billion investment signals a strategic shift that could stabilise the economy diaspora investors increasingly count on.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Supreme Court Signs Landmark MOU with Russia on AI in Courts, Drawing Constitutional Scrutiny
articles.excerpt: CJI Surya Kant's Moscow agreement promises tech collaboration and judicial exchanges, but legal scholars question whether the court overstepped its constitutional role
articles.image_caption: Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, who signed the landmark judicial cooperation MOU with Russia's Supreme Court Chairman Igor Krasnov in Moscow on June 24, 2026.
articles.nri_angle: The MOU's focus on AI-assisted translation and digital court access could significantly benefit NRIs navigating India's judicial system remotely, while the constitutional debate around the agreement reflects broader questions about institutional boundaries that diaspora legal professionals are closely watching.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Quiet Energy Revolution: Domestic Coal Replaces Imports While Renewables Hit Record 17.9% of Generation
articles.excerpt: Power plants designed for imported coal now run on over 50% domestic fuel as solar and wind electricity surges 29% year-on-year, reshaping the country's energy mix
articles.image_caption: A thermal power plant in Uttar Pradesh, India. The country is rapidly switching imported coal-based plants to domestic fuel while renewable energy reaches record generation levels.
articles.image_credit: Wikimedia Commons / Biswarup Ganguly / CC BY 3.0
articles.nri_angle: India's energy transformation has direct implications for NRIs with investments in Indian power companies and the broader economy, as reduced import dependence strengthens the rupee and lowers inflationary pressure on the families they support back home.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: He Left Hyderabad With Nothing. Now He's Buying One of India's Biggest Banks for $5 Billion.
articles.excerpt: Indian-Canadian billionaire Prem Watsa parked $1 billion in government bonds last week. His Fairfax Financial is closing in on IDBI Bank — the largest foreign investment in an Indian bank ever.
articles.image_caption: Prem Watsa, chairman of Fairfax Financial Holdings and an Indian-Canadian billionaire from Hyderabad
articles.nri_angle: Prem Watsa, a first-generation Indian-Canadian immigrant from Hyderabad, is making the largest-ever foreign direct investment in an Indian bank — a powerful symbol of diaspora capital flowing home.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: America Is Rationing Cancer Drugs. The FDA Just Called India for Help.
articles.excerpt: Hospitals can fill barely a third of their orders for a critical chemotherapy drug. Now the FDA's India office has turned to Cipla, Zydus and at least two other Indian manufacturers to plug the gap.
articles.image_caption: Chemotherapy drug infusion components at a hospital — supplies of key cancer drugs like ifosfamide are running critically low across the US
articles.nri_angle: Indian pharma companies are being called upon to fill a critical cancer drug shortage in the US — where Indian-origin physicians and pharmacists disproportionately staff the oncology departments now rationing these same drugs.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Housing Market Just Had Its Best Quarter in Years. NRI Buyers Are Leading the Luxury Charge.
articles.excerpt: Sales surged 19% across India's top nine cities in Q2 2026, with Bengaluru and Hyderabad leading the boom — and overseas Indians are driving the high-end segment that's propping up the entire market.
articles.image_caption: Residential towers rising over Hyderabad, one of India's fastest-growing housing markets in 2026. (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: NRIs are increasingly investing in India's luxury real estate, with favorable exchange rates, post-RERA transparency, and rising prices making Indian property attractive for overseas Indians planning returns, buying for parents, or seeking portfolio diversification.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Iran Just Hit US Bases in Kuwait and Bahrain. Millions of Indians in the Gulf Woke Up to Air-Raid Sirens.
articles.excerpt: The ceasefire that was supposed to end the US-Iran war is in freefall. Iran launched missiles and drones at American military sites across the Gulf on Saturday, Trump threatened to erase Iran, and the Strait of Hormuz is being weaponised again.
articles.image_caption: An oil tanker loading crude oil at a terminal in the Persian Gulf
articles.nri_angle: Over 4.5 million Indians live in Kuwait and Bahrain, the two countries targeted by Iranian strikes. Air-raid sirens and military escalation directly threaten the safety and livelihoods of the Gulf's largest foreign workforce.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Boston Grad, a Dead Cockroach and a 40-Day March. India's Exam Revolt Just Went Mainstream.
articles.excerpt: The Cockroach Janta Party started as a meme. Now CNN is at the protest site, Congress is backing a nationwide campaign, and the government is calling students terrorists.
articles.image_caption: Jantar Mantar in New Delhi, the historic site where students have been protesting since June 20
articles.nri_angle: NRI families watching their children's educational prospects in India dim; the movement's founder is a Boston University graduate who flew back to lead the protests.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Monsoon Is 43% Below Normal. The Government Just Drew Up Emergency Plans for 315 Districts.
articles.excerpt: El Niño is forecast to deliver the weakest rains in 11 years. Farmers are already switching crops, Mumbai is rationing water, and food-price inflation is the elephant in every policy room.
articles.image_caption: A rice paddy field awaits monsoon rains in rural India
articles.nri_angle: NRIs sending remittances to farming families face the downstream impact; weak rains mean lower rural incomes and higher grocery bills for relatives back home.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Central Bank Just Made Dollar Deposits Ridiculously Attractive for NRIs. Here's the Math.
articles.excerpt: The RBI is absorbing all hedging costs on foreign currency deposits, banks are offering 6–7% yields, and with leverage, wealthy NRIs can earn up to 22% annualised returns on a fixed-income product. The window closes September 30.
articles.image_caption: A Reserve Bank of India currency note
articles.nri_angle: NRIs in the US, UK, Canada and Gulf can earn 6-7% on dollar deposits with zero currency risk — and the leverage option offers even higher returns for those with the stomach for it.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Jio, NSE and Zepto Are All Going Public at Once. India's Market Has Never Absorbed ₹70,000 Crore in a Single Window.
articles.excerpt: Three mega IPOs — a telecom giant, a stock exchange monopoly, and a quick-commerce upstart — are about to test whether India's primary market can swallow the biggest listing pipeline in its history.
articles.image_caption: Mukesh Ambani, chairman of Reliance Industries, whose Jio Platforms is filing India's largest-ever IPO
articles.nri_angle: NRIs can invest in Indian IPOs through GIFT City, and Jio's listing gives the diaspora its first chance to directly own shares in the digital utility that connects 500 million Indians.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The Ceasefire Was Twelve Days Old. Then Two More Ships Were Hit and Trump Threatened to Erase Iran.
articles.excerpt: A second tanker attack in the Strait of Hormuz triggered fresh US strikes on Saturday — the worst escalation since the peace deal was signed. Oil markets are closed. India, which just started breathing easier, is holding its breath again.
articles.image_caption: Satellite view of the Strait of Hormuz, the narrow passage between Iran and Oman through which a fifth of the world's oil flows
articles.nri_angle: India imports 85% of its crude oil, and over 200,000 Indian seafarers work on vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz — any escalation directly threatens NRI livelihoods and the cost of everything from petrol to cooking gas back home.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: They Went to America for Better Jobs. Now They’re Coming Home to Fewer Ones.
articles.excerpt: Indian tech hiring has fallen to a 28-month low just as thousands of H-1B professionals are returning. The market that was supposed to catch them isn’t ready.
articles.image_caption: Employees during lunch hour at the Infosys campus in Electronic City, Bengaluru
articles.nri_angle: Directly impacts the 4 million Indian tech workers in the US who are weighing whether to stay amid H-1B hostility or return to an Indian job market that may not have room for them.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Banned Telegram for 150 Million Users to Protect One Exam. A Court Just Said That Was Fine.
articles.excerpt: The Delhi High Court upheld the government's unprecedented week-long shutdown of Telegram ahead of the NEET re-exam — setting a precedent that could reshape how India governs tech platforms.
articles.image_caption: Telegram CEO Pavel Durov, who publicly criticised India's decision to ban his platform for 150 million users
articles.nri_angle: India's willingness to shut down a 150-million-user platform for exam integrity signals a regulatory posture that NRI professionals, diaspora entrepreneurs, and anyone building tech for the Indian market must take seriously.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Won't Export Sugar for Years. El Niño, Ethanol and a Weak Monsoon Are All Squeezing at Once.
articles.excerpt: With inventories at their lowest in three decades, cane farmers switching crops, and ethanol devouring what's left, the world's second-largest sugar producer has no sweetness to spare — and the diaspora's mithai bill is about to go up.
articles.image_caption: Sugarcane harvest in Maharashtra, one of India's largest sugar-producing states
articles.nri_angle: India's sugar export ban will raise global sugar prices and mithai costs for diaspora sweet shops, while a weak monsoon intensifies food inflation and remittance pressure on NRI families.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Washington Is Quietly Closing Every Door That Indian Professionals Use to Stay in America
articles.excerpt: A $100,000 H-1B fee, the end of 'Duration of Status' for students, green card applicants told to go home first, and proposed bills to kill the H-1B-to-green-card pipeline — it's not one policy change, it's a systematic overhaul.
articles.image_caption: The US immigration system is being reshaped on multiple fronts simultaneously
articles.nri_angle: Every major immigration pathway Indian professionals use — student visas, H-1B, green cards — is being tightened simultaneously, affecting over a million Indians in the US pipeline.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's $11-Billion Quick Commerce War Just Got Its Two Biggest Combatants. Kirana Stores Should Be Nervous.
articles.excerpt: Flipkart and Amazon are flooding smaller cities with thousands of dark stores, challenging homegrown startups Blinkit and Zepto in a race that is reshaping how 1.4 billion people shop.
articles.image_caption: A delivery rider on an Indian city street, part of the quick-commerce networks reshaping urban retail
articles.nri_angle: Many NRIs are shareholders in Zomato, Swiggy, and Flipkart, and the quick-commerce model India is perfecting is now being studied and replicated in diaspora markets from the Gulf to Southeast Asia.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India and China Are Talking Again — Quietly, Carefully, and With 100,000 Troops Still on the Border
articles.excerpt: NSA Ajit Doval and Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi met in New Delhi last week and used the word both sides had been avoiding for years: 'normalisation.' But the LAC is still bristling with soldiers.
articles.image_caption: National Security Adviser Ajit Doval, who held talks with Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi in New Delhi
articles.nri_angle: For NRIs in tech, defence, and trade, the India-China dynamic shapes everything from semiconductor supply chains and startup funding to border security and the strategic calculus that determines whether India or China captures the next wave of global manufacturing.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Sent an Entire Field Hospital to Venezuela. It Got There Before Most of the World's Aid Did.
articles.excerpt: Two IAF C-17s carried 35 tonnes of relief supplies, medicines and BHISHM Cubes to earthquake-ravaged La Guaira under 'Operation Amistad' — India's fastest disaster-response deployment to the Western Hemisphere in a decade.
articles.image_caption: An Indian Air Force C-17 Globemaster III, the aircraft type used to deliver humanitarian aid to Venezuela under Operation Amistad
articles.nri_angle: India's rapid humanitarian deployment signals growing global reach and soft power that NRIs can point to — and thousands of Indians in Latin America and the Caribbean are watching the government's crisis-response capacity firsthand.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Just Launched a Trade Probe That Could Sabotage Its Own ₹9-Lakh-Crore Power Grid.
articles.excerpt: The government wants to protect steelmakers from Chinese dumping. But the steel in question goes into every transformer in the country — and India imports 90 percent of it.
articles.image_caption: Power distribution transformers on a utility pole — the kind of equipment whose costs could rise if India imposes anti-dumping duties on imported electrical steel
articles.nri_angle: NRIs with family or investments in India should pay attention: higher transformer costs could delay rural electrification, slow the solar buildout, and raise industrial power tariffs — all of which affect real-estate values, manufacturing returns and quality of life for relatives back home.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: OpenAI Just Hired Uber India's Boss to Run Its Second-Biggest Market. It's Not Messing Around.
articles.excerpt: Prabhjeet Singh, an IIT-IIM alumnus who spent a decade building Uber across South Asia, will become OpenAI's most senior leader in India as the company races to convert ChatGPT's consumer popularity into institutional muscle.
articles.image_caption: The 2026 AI Impact Summit plenary session in New Delhi, where India unveiled its sovereign AI ambitions
articles.nri_angle: India-origin tech professionals worldwide are watching as the AI industry's centre of gravity shifts toward India, where OpenAI's aggressive hiring of IIT-IIM alumni signals career opportunities beyond Silicon Valley.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Adani Just Committed $2.1 Billion to Turn Six Indian Airports Into Small Cities. Mumbai Gets the Biggest Share.
articles.excerpt: The plan calls for hotels, offices, retail, and entertainment districts spanning 655 acres across Mumbai, Navi Mumbai, Ahmedabad, Lucknow, Jaipur, and Guwahati — modelled on Changi, Schiphol, and Incheon.
articles.image_caption: The interior of Mumbai's international terminal, which will anchor Adani's largest airport city investment
articles.nri_angle: For India's 32 million-strong diaspora, airports are the first and last impression of the country — Adani's Changi-inspired plan promises the kind of seamless arrival experience NRIs have long wished for.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Rubio Says Trump Is Coming to India. The Trade Deal, He Says, Is 'on the Last Inches.'
articles.excerpt: In separate White House interviews, America's top diplomat and its envoy to India described the relationship as 'stronger than ever' — and signalled a presidential visit early next year.
articles.image_caption: Prime Minister Narendra Modi meets President Donald Trump at the White House in Washington DC, February 2025
articles.nri_angle: Trade deal terms, H-1B visa policy, and the diplomatic temperature all directly shape the professional and economic lives of 5.1 million Indian Americans.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Is Selling Its Deadliest Weapons to the Gulf. The UAE Is First in Line.
articles.excerpt: After the Iran war exposed the Gulf's dependence on American military hardware, the UAE is in talks to buy India's supersonic BrahMos missile and its AI-powered Akashteer air defence system — a deal that would reshape defence alignments across the Middle East.
articles.image_caption: A BrahMos supersonic cruise missile on display at a DRDO exhibition in India
articles.nri_angle: More than 3.5 million Indians live in the UAE — Gulf security directly affects their safety, livelihoods, and the remittance corridor that sends billions home annually.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Iran Just Claimed Ownership of the World's Most Important Shipping Lane. India Has 200,000 Reasons to Worry.
articles.excerpt: A second tanker was hit on Saturday as Tehran demands ships get Iranian permits to cross the Strait of Hormuz, and Washington warns 'violence will be met with violence.' For India, whose seafarers and oil supply depend on the strait, the ceasefire that was supposed to fix everything is falling apart.
articles.image_caption: US Navy ships transit the Strait of Hormuz, the vital waterway Iran now claims to control
articles.nri_angle: Over 200,000 Indian seafarers work on international vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz — their safety is directly at stake as Iran asserts control over the shipping lane that also carries most of India's crude oil imports.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The Man Who Inspired '3 Idiots' Is About to Join India's Gen Z Revolt. He Says He'll Stop Eating Until the Government Listens.
articles.excerpt: Sonam Wangchuk will begin an indefinite hunger strike at Delhi's Jantar Mantar on Sunday, aligning with the Cockroach Janta Party — a meme-born movement that has CNN, the Wall Street Journal, and 20 million Instagram followers paying attention to India's exam crisis.
articles.image_caption: Sonam Wangchuk, the Ladakhi engineer and climate activist who inspired the film 3 Idiots
articles.nri_angle: The NEET exam crisis undermines the credentials that propelled millions of diaspora professionals into careers abroad, while the CJP's founder is himself a US-educated Indian who returned to lead the movement.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Year Ago, India and Canada Were Expelling Each Other's Diplomats. Now Modi Has Been Invited to Ottawa.
articles.excerpt: Four meetings in under a year, a defence dialogue, a $2.6 billion uranium deal, and a trade target of $50 billion by 2030 — the India-Canada reset is moving at a pace that would have been unthinkable during the Khalistan crisis.
articles.image_caption: Prime Minister Narendra Modi meets Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney on the sidelines of the G7 Summit in Evian, France
articles.nri_angle: For 1.8 million Indians in Canada, the diplomatic thaw means restored consular services, smoother visa processing, and a safer environment after years of Khalistan-related tensions.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Every Forecaster Is Saying the Same Thing: India Is Slowing Down. Here Is Why.
articles.excerpt: S&P, UBS, HDFC Bank, and the RBI all project growth between 6.2% and 6.7% for FY27 — down from 7.7% — as energy stress, a record monsoon deficit, and softening business confidence converge on the world's fastest-growing major economy.
articles.image_caption: The Bombay Stock Exchange building in Mumbai, hub of India's equity markets
articles.nri_angle: NRI investors with equity, bond, and FCNR holdings in India face a shifting landscape as rate hikes, a weakening rupee, and softer corporate earnings rewrite the calculus on where to park overseas savings.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: He Built a Credit-Card App With $1 Million of His Own Money. Now He Runs WhatsApp for 3 Billion People.
articles.excerpt: Meta tapped CRED founder Kunal Shah to lead its biggest messaging platform, invested $900 million in his startup, and handed an Indian entrepreneur the keys to one of the world's most-used products.
articles.image_caption: Kunal Shah, founder of CRED, has been appointed as WhatsApp's new global head by Meta
articles.nri_angle: An Indian entrepreneur who built his companies in India — not through a Western corporate ladder — now runs the messaging app that millions of NRIs rely on daily to stay connected with family and community.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Most Ambitious Trade Deal Goes Live on July 15. If You Work in the UK, Read This.
articles.excerpt: The India-UK Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement eliminates tariffs on 99 per cent of Indian exports, exempts 75,000 Indian professionals from British social security payments, and aims to double bilateral trade to $120 billion by 2030.
articles.image_caption: Union Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal has led India's preparations for the CETA rollout on July 15
articles.nri_angle: The deal directly benefits 75,000 Indian professionals in the UK with a five-year exemption from British social security contributions and opens streamlined entry for Indian workers — reshaping the economic terms under which NRIs in Britain live and work.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Oil Just Had Its Worst Week Since the War Began. India — the World's Third-Largest Importer — Hasn't Cut Fuel Prices by a Single Rupee.
articles.excerpt: Brent crashed 11% to $72, Saudi Aramco restarted its biggest terminal, and an RBI official says $70 oil could push India back to 7% growth. But petrol and diesel remain ₹7.50 a litre above pre-war levels.
articles.image_caption: An oil tanker at sea in the waters near the Middle East
articles.nri_angle: Lower crude prices ease pressure on India's current account, strengthen the rupee, and improve the growth outlook — all of which directly affect the value of NRI remittances, investments, and the cost of flights and goods sent home.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: America Just Decided Who Gets to Use the World's Most Powerful AI. India Had to Ask Not to Be Left Out.
articles.excerpt: Washington restricted Anthropic's Fable 5 and OpenAI's GPT-5.6 over security fears. India's top tech official flew to the Pax Silica Summit to secure a promise: trusted partners won't face 'abrupt cutoffs.'
articles.image_caption: Server racks inside a data centre, the physical infrastructure powering frontier AI models
articles.nri_angle: Indian tech workers in the US are building with these restricted AI models daily, while India's $250-billion IT services industry — the diaspora's biggest employment pipeline — is betting its next growth cycle on uninterrupted access to frontier AI.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Iran Is Offering India $4-a-Barrel Discounts on Crude. So Far, India Isn't Biting.
articles.excerpt: Middlemen from Singapore and Dubai are flooding Indian refiners with offers of cheap Iranian oil after Washington's 60-day sanctions waiver — but full tanks and unclear payment channels are keeping buyers on the sidelines.
articles.image_caption: A crude oil tanker at sea — the kind of vessel now at the centre of renewed Iran-India energy trade talks
articles.nri_angle: Energy prices directly affect the cost of cooking gas, petrol and airline tickets for millions of Indians and shape the inflation outlook that NRIs watch when sending remittances or investing back home.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
